authoredNote: Source written first from the #867 ruling. This is the fixture that FAILS before the fix (the in-method literal reported owner=AnonOwner); the expectation records the post-ruling run's spelling, and the revert mutant below proves it is the fix and not the run that makes it pass.
rationale: M49/M37 #867. kotlin was the outlier: its walker carries only `pClass`, so a literal declared inside a method was attributed to the enclosing CLASS while java/groovy/scala attributed it to the method. Ruled owner = innermost enclosing declaration, and kotlin now derives it from the AST (nearest function_declaration, else pClass). The class-level literal is pinned too: kotlin is the language where a fix could plausibly over-reach and re-own everything to the method, and this fixture would catch that. Kotlin also emits the two 0.5-confidence `overrides` edges from the anon members to their supertypes; they are deliberately NOT pinned here (#866/#867 owe nothing to that class, and pinning them would freeze an unrelated guess).
